_documentation: The ONE place real account names are declared. See README.md beside this file. Both the installed workstation disk and a persistent Controller's durable directory accounts follow this file; the domain_controller role names contract ROLES only (homelab_ad_directory_accounts in ../inventory/group_vars/controllers.yml) and renders the rest from here. Copying this template changes nothing: `principals` is empty and there is no `additional_standard_users`, so every account keeps the synthetic name from workstations/identity_lifecycle.json and its positional directory UID, and the acceptance gates are unaffected. The durable-account paths refuse it until standard_user, daily_administrator and domain_administrator are all named here. Fill `principals` in to name your real accounts. Keys beginning with an underscore are documentation and are ignored by the loader; every other unknown key is refused.
_example_uid_numbers: Optional, per directory role: add "uid_number" beside "name" to pin that role's directory uidNumber, as in _example_pinned_principals. An unpinned role keeps 10000 + its position (standard_user 10000, daily_administrator 10001, domain_administrator 10002). Every number must be a JSON integer from 10000 to 60000, must not be 10512 or 10513 (the Domain Admins and Domain Users gids), and must differ from every other account's number, positional defaults included: a clash is refused, never shifted. local_rescue is a local account and may not be pinned.
_example_additional_standard_users_docum: Optional top-level list `additional_standard_users`: people with no contract role, each an ordinary standard directory account -- never Domain Admins, never workstation sudo. Only the durable paths (make homelab-factory-persistent-accounts and the domain_controller role) create them; no acceptance gate stages or checks them. Each needs a name (same rules as a directory role: at most 20 characters, not a reserved directory or system account, distinct from every name in principals) and an explicit uid_number.
